item.title: Meta is using the Linux scheduler designed for Valve's Steam Deck on its servers
item.description:
📝 Meta Is Using The Linux Scheduler Designed For Valve's Steam Deck On Its Servers Written by Michael Larabel in Linux Kernel on 23 December 2025 at 06:10 AM EST. 13 Comments An interesting anecdote from this month's Linux Plumbers Conference in Tokyo is that Meta (Facebook) is using the Linux scheduler originally designed for the needs of Valve's Steam Deck. Meta has found that the scheduler can actually adapt and work very well on the hyperscaler's large servers.
🔗 Read more: https://www.phoronix.com/news/Meta-SCX-LAVD-Steam-Deck-Server

item.title: Towards a secure peer-to-peer app platform for Clan
item.description:
📝 Meanwhile in the FOSS world, it’s still extremely common to run software with full access to the user’s account. Meanwhile local software often doesn’t have a global database, but when it does, it can be impossible to make it multi-instance without advanced knowledge; Commercial apps come with their own always-online remote servers. For our platform development, we have indeed adopted muvm (after submitting some changes that make it more useful for us), combining it with namespace-based Bubblewrap to make a script that runs NixOS system closures in microVMs.
🔗 Read more: https://clan.lol/blog/towards-app-platform-vmtech/

item.title: Stop Slopware
item.description:
📝 If someone thinks your project is slopware, don’t despair, you have a chance to fix your work and prove them wrong. You have better things to do with your time; and yet, it’s important to inform project authors why their work isn’t being received well. For a more detailed discussion, consider reading the article your project sucks.
🔗 Read more: https://stopslopware.net/
